result:
I graded submission s2 for quiz 0001 and wrote `grades/0001-s2.json`, with feedback on every item. You got 3 correct, 2 partial and 1 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | Correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | Correct | The model outputs a tool request, not the result. |
| q3 | Wrong (M6) | A stuck agent won't eventually fix itself. You need a stopping condition, such as a step limit. |
| q4 | Partial (M4) | 4 is the right count, but you said the model "runs" the tools. It only requests them, and the program runs them. |
| q5 | Correct | You gave both parts: the result goes back as the next input, so the model can decide its next step. |
| q6 | Partial | The name helps, but the model picks a tool from the whole description: name, purpose and parameters. |

**Summary:** You have the core of the loop. Fix two things next:
- **Who runs the tools:** the model requests them and the program runs them.
- **Stopping:** an agent needs a stopping condition, and it also protects your model budget.

**Next step:** Write a three-sentence description for `check_calendar` covering what it does, when to use it and what its parameters mean. Then we can move on to context and memory.

I also wrote `learning-records/0003-model-requests-program-runs-and-stopping.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. Submission s1 is still ungraded. I can grade it too if you want to compare the two attempts.
